cards.text: Jesus is in Jerusalem now, and He walks into the temple courts. There are people in there SELLING. Friend, this is God's house, and somebody set up a checkout lane.

cards.question: Jesus walks into the temple courts and finds people selling there. What does He do?

answers.text: He begins to drive them out
He sits down and watches them
He asks the priests about it

cards.text: And Jesus doesn't just drive them out. He tells them what's written in Scripture about God's house, and friend, when your next line is Scripture, nobody is winning that argument.

cards.question: God's house is meant to be a house of prayer. What does Jesus tell the sellers they've made it?

cards.text: After that, Jesus is teaching at the temple EVERY. SINGLE. DAY. Meanwhile the chief priests, the scribes and the leaders of the people are intent on killing Him.

cards.question: The chief priests, scribes and leaders of the people want to kill Jesus. Why can't they find a way to do it?

answers.text: All the people hang on His words
His disciples stand guard around Him

cards.text: One day Jesus is teaching the people in the temple courts and proclaiming the gospel, when up walk the chief priests, the scribes AND the elders. Friend, that's the whole group chat showing up in person, and NOBODY brought cookies.

cards.question: The chief priests, scribes and elders walk up to Jesus in the temple courts. What do they ask Him?

answers.text: By what authority He does these things
Why His disciples do not fast
How long He plans to stay in the city

cards.text: Jesus doesn't hand them an answer. He tells them He's got a question for them too, and friend, they called this meeting and now HE'S the one asking the questions.

cards.question: Jesus has a question of His own for the chief priests, scribes and elders. What's it about?

cards.text: That's John the Baptist, who went all around the Jordan preaching a baptism of repentance (Luke 3:3). Jesus asks them whether John's baptism was from heaven or from men, and friend, that's just two options. How hard could it be?
The leaders huddle up and talk it over among themselves. I know that huddle, friend: that's coworkers rewriting ONE email to the boss for forty-five minutes so nothing comes back on them.

cards.question: The leaders figure that if they say John's baptism was from heaven, Jesus will ask why they didn't believe John.
If the leaders say John's baptism was from men, they'll have trouble with the crowd, because the people are convinced John was a ___.
If the leaders say John's baptism was from men, what do they think the people will do to them?
The leaders have talked it over. What do they finally tell Jesus about John's baptism?
Since the leaders won't say where John's baptism came from, Jesus goes ahead and tells them where His own authority comes from.

cards.text: Jesus replies, "Neither will I tell you by what authority I am doing these things." They gave Him nothing, and friend, nothing is EXACTLY what they get back.

findings.problem: The card retells Jesus driving out the sellers, which comes from Luke 19:45, as well as His declaration in Luke 19:46. Its citation covers only Luke 19:46, so it is narrower than the verses the card uses.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: the background on John, Jesus' question with its accompanying comment, and "How hard could it be?" It needs to be reduced to one or two sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Seven of the ten choice cards are multiple choice, including the first five choices in a row. With only two true-or-false cards and one fill-in-the-blank card, multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
